h: Swinging Into a Proper Essex Day Out
p: If this is your first time at a Puttshack, here's the gist. The company was set up by the brothers behind Topgolf, and their big idea was to bring that same tech-driven fun to mini golf. Every ball is tracked, so the scoring is automatic, and the holes can react to your shots with lights, sounds and twists that make even a wobbly putt entertaining.

Some tips for a good round. Have a look at how the scoring screens work on the first hole, so you're not puzzled halfway through. Take your time on the trickier holes, as rushing usually ends in a ricochet. Rotate who goes first on each hole to keep things fair, and if you're with friends who take games very seriously, agree some friendly stakes before you start.
Families should check the age policy before booking, as Puttshack venues commonly restrict children at certain times, especially later in the evening.

There's more to the area than shopping. Grays Beach Riverside Park on the Thames has a play area and is a nice spot to stretch your legs and watch the ships go by. History lovers can head to Tilbury Fort, an English Heritage site with impressive defences overlooking the river, or Coalhouse Fort near East Tilbury. Both offer a very different side to Thurrock from the shopping centre, and they're a short drive away.
Remember, school holidays and weekends are busy at Lakeside, so plan your journey with time to spare and book that tee time well ahead.
